last_email.angle: Weekly check-in: the 10-minute counting review from the plan.

today.body:
After you shut down your computer at the end of the workday, write a single line in your notebook – “Tally: X, IF‑then uses: Y, Pages read: Z” – and stop. Floor version: open the notebook and scribble the line in under 30 seconds.

Reason: the cue‑action pair creates an automatic habit loop and the brief visual note gives an immediate completion signal (evidence: mixed).

Español del día (new): "¿Puede enviarme el reporte?" – use it when you need a colleague to send you a document.

Note from M: Let me know if the cue works for you, or we can adjust it.

b.advice: Tie the Sunday check‑in to a concrete cue you already do – for example, after you shut down your computer at the end of the workday, say “Check‑in time” and open the notebook. The tiny action is to write a single line: “Tally: X, IF‑then uses: Y, Pages read: Z”. Keep it under 30 seconds. The immediate reward is a brief mental note of progress (“done”) and a small physical cue, such as clicking a check‑box or moving a sticky‑note to a ‘done’ pile, which reinforces the habit through a clear completion signal. This combines an implementation‑intention (cue → action) with a visual completion cue, both shown to boost self‑monitoring compliance.

t.lesson: After you shut down your computer tonight, open a browser, log into GitHub, and click “New repository”. Name it “qa-docs” and click Create. That’s all – under 30 seconds and no code needed. It gives you a place to store SOPs and checklists that the whole team can access and version‑control.
